Quality assurance (QA) is a process that ensures your products or services are meeting the standards you’ve put in place. Through continuous monitoring and evaluation, organisations can identify any problems or gaps in service and take necessary actions to improve. hits.title: Insurance multi-firm review of outcomes monitoring under the ...
hits.snippet:
Some firms had made considerable efforts to build an approach to monitoring under this heading, which included data points from a number of sources (as per above). The approach often included firms adapting their internal Quality Assurance (QA) processes and methodology to have a clear focus on monitoring customer understanding (amongst other Duty outcomes). This included clearly mapping a wide range of customer journeys so that the consumer understanding outcome could be tested methodically [...] This was sometimes developed as a new initiative, or sometimes adapted from existing Quality Assurance frameworks. In the good examples we saw, the analysis from such testing was clearly and directly linked to the four Duty outcomes. We saw evidence that a clear testing framework led to good identification of poor outcomes, and such an approach allowed root causes to be identified and rectified.

### Poor practice: repackaging existing data [...] Some firms were able to demonstrate clear thinking about the categories of data they required, such as: service level agreement (SLA) compliance, product performance data, second- and third-line reviews, customer feedback, internal quality assurance, complaints analysis, process completion, product governance findings, employee surveys and deep dive analysis. Firms that had demonstrated such thinking were able to provide more meaningful and comprehensive insights on customer outcomes.
